coupling: The defect is split across two commits in gf_ac4_substream_info_obj() (src/media_tools/av_parsers.c), and only their composition is unsafe. (1) c1e0ad6 'Fix the assignment of n_signals' replaces the if/else chain that mapped n_objects_code to n_signals with a direct lookup into N_OBJECTS_CODE_TO_NUM_OBJECTS and, to keep that new lookup total over the full 3-bit domain (0..7), pads the table from 6 to 8 entries. Read alone this is correct maintenance: the table now covers every value the unguarded 3-bit read can produce, so the lookup is in bounds for all inputs. (2) 278c474 'fuzz: ac4 mem fixes' adds a bounds guard before the *other* user of the same table (the dynamic-objects loop) and, as part of the same fuzz cleanup, restores the table initializer to the spec's 6 defined codes. Read alone this is also correct maintenance: in the tree this commit actually sees, n_signals is still computed by the if/else chain (reserved codes fall to the else branch), the only table user left is the loop it just guarded with GF_ARRAY_LENGTH, and every reserved value is rejected before any indexing. Neither commit exposes a bug on its own: the edit-1-only tree (8-entry table, unguarded lookup) and the edit-2-only tree (identical in content to the original batch) both run the PoC cleanly under the sanitizer. The bug exists only at the composed tip, where the unguarded 'n_signals = N_OBJECTS_CODE_TO_NUM_OBJECTS[substream->n_objects_code]' introduced by commit 1 survives while the table it indexes has been shrunk to 6 entries by commit 2: for the reserved codes 6 and 7 the lookup reads past the 24-byte stack array. A correct fix is necessarily non-local: reverting commit 2's table shrink alone reintroduces non-spec values in a table that other code treats as spec-defined; guarding commit 1's lookup alone leaves the invariant split across two sites so the next reader of either commit re-breaks it. The reviewer must recognize that commit 1 created an unguarded consumer whose safety depended on the 8-entry width, and that commit 2 silently removed that width while guarding only its own use site - the fix (guard the lookup, or make the reserved-code mapping explicit) has to reason about both diffs together.
